claim_type: universally quantified over an infinite domain; finite experiments are scoped corroboration only

exact_statement.conclusion: (E3): D-Reg_T <= beta lambda ||u_1||^2 + d(1+BR) log(1 + R^2 (sum_t beta^{T-t})/(d lambda (1+BR))) + (beta/(1-beta)) P_T^beta + ((1-beta)/beta) d(1+BR) T. Theorem 4: the Algorithm 1 two-layer ensemble over beta_i = eta_i/(1+eta_i) attains O(dB log(BT) + sqrt(dBT P_T^{beta*})).
exact_statement.quantifiers: for all T >= 1; beta in (0,1); lambda > 0; d >= 1; ||z_t|| <= R; comparators ||u_t|| <= B; decisions unconstrained in R^d

informal_statement: Discounted AIOLI for online logistic regression attains a dynamic regret bound whose dependence on the comparator norm B is only through the factor (1+BR), i.e. linear -- avoiding the e^B degradation that proper online Newton step suffers.
known_power_limitation: 3 of 6 weakened bounds cannot be broken (drop_B_dependence 98.9%, zinkevich_path 93.4%, halve_log_term 51.1% of the slack they need). Structural, not budget: a moving comparator makes term3 = (beta/(1-beta))P_T^beta dominate by ~3 orders of magnitude, while a static comparator makes improper AIOLI beat the comparator outright and regret go negative. Consequence: (E3) is corroborated only up to the constant in its log term and its stated B-dependence; those parts are UNTESTED, not confirmed.
non_circularity: No formula-derived quantity is used as the primary evidence for the formula it comes from. Where a finite experiment cannot establish a universally quantified statement, the verdict is BLOCKED rather than VERIFIED.

paper.anchor: Section 3.2, Theorem 3 (explicit bound E3) and Theorem 4 (asymptotic rate for the Algorithm 1 ensemble)
paper.title: Dynamic Regret via Discounted-to-Dynamic Reduction with Applications to Curved Losses and Adam Optimizer

verdict_rule: VERIFIED requires no violations AND all links AND every weakened bound broken. The last fails by measurement, so the verdict is BLOCKED.

verification_design.algorithm: the Section 3.2 implicit update solved as the genuine implicit problem by damped Newton with backtracking and PER-ROUND convergence certification -- not a logistic-SGD proxy. Undamped Newton diverged here (dreg 1.4e8); that was a solver bug, not a finding, which is why convergence is certified.
verification_design.b_dependence: AIOLI vs a real ONS baseline over B in [0.5,10], stated in LEVELS against an explicit linear-in-B reference because AIOLI is improper and its regret legitimately goes negative, making ratio-of-growth statistics meaningless
verification_design.calibration: 2336-evaluation adversarial search (random + 3 hill-climbing rounds), identical budget against the true bound and all 6 weakened bounds, with a POWER RATIO recorded per control = (bound removed)/(slack available); >1 is needed to fire
verification_design.sweep: 680 configurations over 6 data generators x 7 comparator strategies, including per_round_optimal (u_t on the ball boundary aligned with y_t z_t, the exact per-round minimiser and hence the strongest admissible comparator)

what_would_falsify_it: one assumption-satisfying instance with dynamic regret strictly exceeding (E3)
